C0.quote: we propose a novel famliy of randomized voting rules based on the well-known Condorcet method
C0.note: Randomized voting rules aggregating votes; axiomatic analysis

C1.quote: We prove that all of our rules satisfy absolute monotonicity, lexi-participation
C1.note: Satisfaction of axioms, incompatibility with DP. Tight DP bounds are also axiom-like properties of the rule. Strategyproofness axiom is a property, but the SB type is not coded because there is no modelled strategic agent in the main analysis.

C2.1.quote: the vote of voter j is a linear order

C2.2.quote: the vote of voter j is a linear order j ∈ L(A)

C2.3.quote: voters submit their preferences over a set of alternatives
C2.3.note: Preferences mentioned; in strategyproofness definitions 'benefit herself'

C2.4.quote: voters submit their preferences over a set of alternatives
C2.4.note: Preferences and votes used interchangeably ('(preference) profile'); no statement about misreporting or sincerity, rule applied directly.

C3.1.quote: no voter can benefit herself in the sense of stochastic dominance
C3.1.note: SD-SP and participation are axioms comparing profiles; no analysis models voters strategically submitting differing inputs.

C3.2.note: No statement that voters submit held preferences.

C4.1.note: Strategyproofness uses stochastic dominance on rankings; no utility link to voters is used. Utility loss is mentioned only for prior work.

C5.1.note: Pareto efficiency is evaluated as an axiom in results.

C5.2.quote: a k b holds for all k ∈ N
C5.2.note: Pareto dominance defined on submitted rankings; no statement relating to held attitudes.

VOT.note: Voters appear only via profiles; axioms compare profiles, no agent takes action in the model.

C8.1.note: NA: no STRAT or MIXED type

claims.quote: Designing private voting rules is an important and pressing problem for trustworthy democracy.
there is little motivation for an adversary to manipulate the voting process
our results suggest that CMLAP outperforms CMEXP in all aspects

C9.1.note: Claims about democracy and about which mechanism performs better; the paper's strongest claim concerns rule comparison.

C9.2.quote: there is little motivation for an adversary to manipulate the voting process
C9.2.note: The manipulation-incentive claim needs an assumption about adversary/voter behaviour and about what they know and want, and about how votes relate to held preferences; none are stated in the model.
